items.title: Man wanted after stabbing in Mississauga leaves victim seriously injured
items.summary: A man is wanted after a stabbing in Mississauga early Saturday morning left one person with serious injuries. m. A victim was located and transported to a trauma centre for treatment. An update on their condition has not been released. Police have not provided additional information about the victim, including their age, whether they are male or female or their place of residence. It is also unclear whether the stabbing was targeted or if the suspect and victim were known to each other. The suspect is described as a Black man with a height of 5-foot-11. He has cornrows and speaks with a Caribbean accent. He was last seen wearing a black T-shirt with red stripes and black shoes. Investigators say the suspect fled the area in a dark-coloured minivan. Anyone with information is asked to contact Peel Regional Police at 905-453-2121.

items.title: Police arrest UK man at airport months after armed Mississauga carjacking
items.summary: A 24-year-old man from the United Kingdom has been arrested after Peel Regional Police allege he fled Canada following an armed carjacking in Mississauga earlier this year. According to investigators, the suspect returned to Toronto on an international flight on July 16 and was arrested upon landing at Pearson Airport on an outstanding Canada-wide warrant. The charges stem from a carjacking that occurred on Feb. m. in the area of Torbram Road and Derry Road East. Police say the victim was sitting inside a commercial vehicle when two masked suspects approached armed with handguns. The suspects allegedly pointed the firearms at the victim before forcing him from the vehicle and stealing it. Following an investigation by Peel Regional Police’s Central Robbery Bureau, officers identified Raheem Hartley, 24, of the United Kingdom, as one of the alleged suspects. Investigators say Hartley left Canada shortly after the carjacking. A Canada-wide warrant for his arrest was issued in December 2025 after police determined he had fled the country. When Hartley returned to Canada on July 16, officers arrested him at Toronto Pearson International Airport. Hartley has been charged with robbery, disguise with intent, and use of an imitation firearm while committing an offence.

items.title: Heat warning slows down express trains at Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga
items.summary: Passengers riding Union Pearson Express trains between Mississauga and Toronto on Friday afternoon might notice several delays due to a heat warning issued by Canada’s weather agency, transit officials say. The UP Express moves passengers between Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga and Union Station in downtown Toronto. Transit officials said to customers in an online post that “a heat warning from Environment Canada is in effect today. We are required to run trains at slower speeds. m. ” UP Express officials have also given a heads-up to customers that the trains will be replaced by GO buses the weekend of Aug. 15-16 due to planned construction on the line. When operating without delays, the express trains transport riders between Canada’s biggest and busiest airport and Union Station in downtown Toronto in just under 30 minutes, making several stops along the way. m. between downtown Toronto and Pearson. Officials at Metrolinx said earlier the express train service “has become an integral part of transit in Toronto, having served more than 26 million passengers” since its inception in 2015. In what at the time was the “first dedicated express air-rail link service in North America,” the UP Express took its first passengers between Pearson and Union Station in downtown Toronto on June 6, 2015, Ontario transit officials said earlier.
